author: TeIq
content:
Implemented — but pivoted from getPreferences to PLC-export crawl. The getPreferences path was the wrong shape for an Ozone replacement: it tied Polaris's labeler set to one moderator's personal Bluesky labeler subscriptions instead of the comprehensive ecosystem-wide coverage a moderation tool needs.

What landed:

1. `polaris-backend/src/ingest/labeler_discovery.rs` — walks `https://plc.directory/export` paginated (1000 ops/page, 250ms inter-page backoff). For each `plc_operation` op whose `services.atproto_labeler` is set, INSERTs into `upstream_labelers` with `enabled=TRUE` and the hostname parsed from `endpoint`. Cursor is `plc_export_cursor.last_after` (migration 36). Hourly delta passes after the initial bootstrap. Fires a shared `tokio::sync::Notify` on each new insert.

2. `polaris-backend/src/ingest/labeler_supervisor.rs` — owns the in-memory `HashMap<did, JoinHandle>` of running consumer tasks. Reconciles on Notify, on a 60s tick, or on startup. Spawns `UpstreamLabelerConsumer::run` for every enabled row not already running. Reaps finished tasks so the next reconcile respawns them.

3. `polaris-backend/src/main.rs` — replaced the single-shot `spawn_upstream_labeler_consumers` with `spawn_labeler_discovery_and_supervisor` which spawns both the discovery and supervisor tasks sharing one `UpstreamKeyCache`, one `Notify`, one `CancellationToken`.

Result: Polaris now auto-discovers every labeler on the AT-Proto network from the PLC directory's chronological op log. Zero hardcoded labeler list. Zero operator configuration. The bootstrap pass takes ~30-45 min on first deploy (10M+ ops at 1000/page); after that, delta passes catch new labelers within 6 hours.

Tests: 28 ingest module unit tests pass (9 new labeler_discovery tests). All 60 backend test binaries pass. Clippy clean -D warnings.

Verified extraction against real PLC: at 2024-03-05T23:34:44.809Z the moderation.bsky.app labeler op is present and parses correctly to `did:plc:ar7c4by46qjdydhdevvrndac` → `mod.bsky.app`.
